title: "MBeRCS Water Quality Explorer"

The **South Florida Ecosystem Restoration (SFER)** program, run by NOAA in
collaboration with the Southeast U.S. Marine Biodiversity Observation Network
(SEUS MBON), conducts bi-monthly research cruises across the Florida Keys and
the west Florida shelf. Those cruises collect in-situ physical,
biogeochemical, bio-optical, genomic, planktonic and harmful-algal-bloom
observations to evaluate the drivers of ecosystem variability and change.

This site is a working exploration of the **discrete water-quality** portion of
that effort — the **MBeRCS** dataset — focused on the spatial and temporal
patterns that support monitoring of Florida's coastal and marine resources.

::: {.callout-note}
**Data source.** All pages read a single file, `../data/SFER_data.csv`, which is
downloaded from
[`Ecosystem-Assessment-Lab/SFER`](https://github.com/Ecosystem-Assessment-Lab/SFER/blob/main/DATA/SFER_data.csv).
It is *not* committed to this repository — see
[README.md](README.md#data) for the one-line download command.
:::

## At a glance

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sfer_common as sfer
import pandas as pd

sfer.style()
df = sfer.load()
analytes = [c for c in sfer.ANALYTES if df[c].notna().any()]
```

- **Sampling span:** `{python} f"{df.datetime.min():%B %Y} \u2013 {df.datetime.max():%B %Y}"` (`{python} df.year.nunique()` calendar years)
- **Cruises:** `{python} df.cruise_id.nunique()` across `{python} df.vessel.nunique()` vessels
- **Sampling stations:** `{python} f"{df.station.nunique():,}"`
- **Discrete samples:** `{python} f"{len(df):,}"`
- **Analytes:** `{python} len(analytes)`
- **Depth classes:** `{python} f"{(df.depth_class=='Surface').sum():,} surface, {(df.depth_class=='Mid').sum():,} mid, {(df.depth_class=='Bottom').sum():,} bottom"`

## Reading the data

The CSV is a *tidy, one-row-per-discrete-sample* table. Key columns:

- `keyfield`, `cruise_id`, `datetime` — sample identity and time;
- `lat_dec`, `lon_dec`, `station`, `station_type` (`C` / `F`, as coded upstream)
  — location;
- `depth`, `depth_class` (`Surface` / `Mid` / `Bottom`), `cast`, `nisk_start`,
  `nisk_end` — sampling depth and Niskin-bottle metadata;
- one column per analyte (`temp`, `sal`, `o2_ctd`, `o2_disc`, `nh4`, `po4`,
  `no3_no2`, `no3`, `no2`, `si`, `chl`, `pheo`) plus a matching `*_flag`
  quality-control column.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Caveats.** Values are reported as-is; the `*_flag` codebook is maintained by
the upstream program and is *not* bundled with the CSV, so flagged values are
shown but not automatically removed. A handful of physically impossible values
(e.g. an `o2_ctd` reading in the thousands of mg/L) are also present and are
handled conservatively in the plots.
:::
